summary: Plausible and not a retry. Done results show single-kernel Triton paths report about what their kernel takes, while the two-node nvjet+splitKreduce qkv_gate path reports 2-4 us more than its kernel sum. A one-node kernel at the measured BLOCK_N=64 Triton bandwidth (3.73 TB/s) lands around 10.5-12 us against today's 13.8-14.4 us. One run is interpretable on its own because only qkv_gate m<=32 changes and the profile names the new kernel's time.
justification: Mechanism: qkv_gate m<=32 is pure weight streaming (37.7 MB, floor 7.9 us). Today it is two graph nodes. Reported vs profiled kernel sums: decode_1 14.4 vs 10.8+1.7; decode_16 13.8 vs 8.1+1.7; decode_32 14.3 vs 10.2+1.8; verify_1 14.0 vs 9.2+2.0. Every single-kernel Triton result in done/ has reported close to profiled: unpooler-full-triton-skinny-m32 decode_16 18.0 vs 18.0, qkv-gate-triton-skinny-m32 decode_1 22.6 vs 22.0. So the 'reported-minus-kernel gap' is real and tied to the extra node, and folding the reduce into one launch should remove most of it. The bandwidth premise also has evidence: the BLOCK_N=64 Triton stream measured 3.73 TB/s on unpooler (67 MB in 18.0 us), and 37.7 MB at that rate is 10.1 us. The 144-CTA split-K grid answers the in-flight-bytes failure of the full-K BLOCK_N=16 kernel (0.924x, ~1.6 TB/s). Its ~9 MB in flight is above Little's law for HBM3e. The ticket semaphore does not spin, so it cannot deadlock even if CTAs are not co-resident. It is graph-safe: counters reset in-kernel, workspace and counters are allocated in prepare(), there are no host syncs, and it branches only on m. The fixed 0..3 summation order makes it deterministic. Shape expectations: faster at m=1/8/16 and flat-or-slower at m=32 matches the per-shape evidence. BLOCK_M=32 Triton tiles were slower than nvjet on unpooler decode_32: 19.8 and 21.9 us vs 18.5. m=128/256 untouched is correct. Payoff in score terms: about 2-3 us off a roughly 55 us decode_1 load is about 4-5% on that load, and four of six loads are affected. That is above the about 1.5% CI half-width and well above the qkv_gate decode_1 cell's run-to-run drift (0.981-1.025 across five master-equivalent runs). WEAKEST LINK: carrying the 3.73 TB/s unpooler number over to a kernel half its size with shorter per-CTA streams. Unpooler streamed 67 MB over 18 us. Here each CTA does only 16 K-steps of 256-byte row segments (BLOCK_K=128 vs unpooler's 256), so pipeline ramp, first-byte latency and the semaphore tail (last-arriving CTA per column reloads 4 partials and stores) are a larger share. The 12 SMs hosting two of the 144 CTAs may also set the tail. If effective bandwidth falls to about 3.0 TB/s plus about 1 us of epilogue and ramp, the kernel is about 13.5 us and the result is flat. Second weakest: the 'nvjet is at 4.66 TB/s' figure (8.1 us at m=16) is a profile number that varies 8.0-10.8 us run to run on identical code. Don't read it as the cold-L2 bar. The reported 13.8-14.4 us is the bar.
confounders: sglang-gemm-dispatch-parity (965b046): this defines the qkv_gate path being replaced, and the baseline uses the same dispatch, so the measured delta is Triton vs nvjet with no interaction. qkv_gate m>=128 stays on it as a control. Not a confounder.

router-triton-hilo-fused-control-splitk-all-m (dba4ffd): this is the design template only. The router shapes, kernel and state are untouched, so router cells are a clean control. Its own result logged a 'loss' on qkv_gate decode_1 (0.981) with unchanged qkv code, which shows that cell drifts by about ±2% from noise. Gains or losses on qkv_gate under about 3% should not be attributed. The expected about 15-20% cell effect is far outside that.
router-hilo-at-m8 (f9dc05d): router-only threshold, superseded by the all-m Triton router. No shared launch sequence, memory or numerics with qkv_gate. Not a confounder.
interference: No companion is warranted. Only the qkv_gate m<=32 cells change, and each scored shape is timed as its own graph after an L2 flush, so a landed hypothesis cannot leak into these cells through cache or launch-sequence effects. Reverting or retuning a landed item would not change what this run measures. The run is still interpretable whichever way it goes. A gain is unambiguous, since only one new kernel is on the path. A loss or a split result can be read from the per-shape table plus the profile's single-kernel duration: kernel time well above 10 us means bandwidth or occupancy, and the hypothesis already pre-registers the one-axis retunes (SPLIT_K=8/num_stages=3 or BLOCK_N=128/SPLIT_K=8); a slowdown only at m=32 means the BLOCK_M=32 penalty and the follow-up is restricting to m<=16. The one ambiguity a companion could resolve is epilogue cost vs streaming cost. A fair control for that (atomic_add into a zeroed fp32 buffer) would add a memset and a cast node and reintroduce the very gap under test, so it would not isolate cleanly. It is better run only if the primary comes back flat with a kernel time near 11-12 us.
rules_flags: Workspace hygiene (fresh-inputs rule): state['qkv_ws'] persists across calls. Every value the reduce reads must be written earlier in the same launch. Either store all BLOCK_M rows of the partial (masked rows as 0) and reduce them, or mask the store and the reduce loads with the same offs_m < m mask. Never let rows >= m from a previous call's x be read into anything that reaches the output, even masked out later. Same for m=1 inside a BLOCK_M=16 tile.

Scalar atomic lowering: make sure tl.atomic_add(cnt_ptr + pid_n, 1, sem='acq_rel', scope='gpu') on a scalar pointer is issued once per CTA (Triton predicates scalar atomics to one thread and broadcasts the result) on the installed Triton version. If every thread issues it, the counter reaches 128*SPLIT_K, the ticket test silently selects no or multiple reducers, and output is garbage or racy. Check the PTX for a single predicated atom.acq_rel.gpu, or rely on the m=1 qkv_gate test plus the every-call correctness check to fail loudly.

Memory ordering: plain partial stores -> tl.debug_barrier() (bar.sync) -> gpu-scope acq_rel atomic by one thread is the CUTLASS-style semaphore pattern and is sound under PTX cumulativity. The reducer must read partials with .cg (L2) after the acquiring atomic, and the broadcast ticket must not be hoisted above the barrier. Not a rule break, but any race shows up as a correctness failure on a timed call, which fails the run.

Graph capture: fine. No host sync, no input-value branching (the ticket is device-side data, not a host branch), torch.empty out is allocated in the normal way. The counter is reset in-kernel by the reducer and is zero after prepare()'s warm-up. A launch that never runs to completion is the only way to leave it dirty, and that cannot happen in a replayed graph.

Precision: bf16 x and W, fp32 tl.dot accumulate, one bf16 cast. Same precision class as cuBLAS. Single-nonzero power-of-two rows stay exact because each partial is an exact fp32 sum of exact products. Weights are not repacked or converted. No flag.

Shared state if pooler-triton-splitk2-blockn64-semaphore also lands: the counters and workspace must be separate state keys (or indexed per layer). Two layers sharing one counter array would corrupt each other only if they ran concurrently, which they do not, but separate keys keep it obviously safe.
open_questions: Does the installed Triton lower the scalar atomic_add with sem/scope to a single-thread atom.acq_rel.gpu? Dump the PTX in the attempt file.

Smem per CTA at num_stages=4: weight 16 KB + x 4 KB (BLOCK_M=16) or 8 KB (BLOCK_M=32) per stage is 80-96 KB, so 2 CTAs/SM fit in 228 KB only if Triton does not add epilogue scratch. Confirm the occupancy claim from the compiled kernel's shared-memory size.

Is BLOCK_K=128 (256-byte row segments from the [N, K] weight) chosen on purpose over unpooler's BLOCK_K=256 (512-byte segments, 8 K-steps per 2048 slice)? If the result is flat, that is a third cheap retune axis.
If m=32 regresses while m<=16 gains, restrict the route to m<=16 rather than retuning BLOCK_M=32. The per-shape table will show it directly.
If both this and the pooler semaphore hypothesis gain, merge them into one parametrized kernel with per-layer state keys, as the hypothesis itself suggests.
